sections.title: Observational reach, nonmetric time, and beginnings
sections.rationale: The opening scientific limits and the nonmetric alternative jointly test whether evidence for a finite-looking past warrants a global beginning.

sections.title: Timeless grounding and physical totality
sections.rationale: The parties dispute whether temporal events can be grounded in a timeless physical substructure and what that implies for the beginning of the physical totality.

sections.title: Causal scope, design, and motion relevance
sections.rationale: This section gathers the motion-level burden, the scope of causation in physics, and whether design of an ordered state establishes a cause or beginning of the physical totality.

sections.title: The causal principle and its proposed symmetry breaker
sections.rationale: The initial deductive defense of a cause for beginnings and the efficient-cause reply to material parity form one direct exchange.

sections.title: Material parity, explanatory reasons, and causal types
sections.rationale: The extended questioning develops distinct support for material dependence, reasons without efficient causes, transformations, and the parties' final clarification of causal scope.

sections.title: First-cause dependence and physical scope
sections.rationale: Regress termination and the proposed physical, nonmetric first-cause alternative concern whether a first member establishes a cause beyond physical reality.

sections.title: Agency, control, and withholding
sections.rationale: The remaining exchange tests whether origination and alternative control require personal agency, especially when nonmetric time supplies no measurable waiting interval.

selectionBalanceAudit.rationale: The section differences reflect source-required distinct replies, not a symmetry target. Material parity contains four separate con developments: field-based support, reasons without efficient causes, the material-only transformation parallel, and the final motion-level parity clarification. Agency contains three distinct pro steps—initial agency derivation, no-deliberation reply, and modal withholding account—against Linford's distinct nonmetric-withholding objection. No move is duplicated to balance counts.

sections.rationale: The fourth con row is source-required because burden framing is placed elsewhere and these four cards separately cover the opening global-observation case, opening nonmetric alternative, theorem-based global-structure reply, and direct no-length clarification.
The initial possibility, developed model, A/B/C clarification, and two pro event replies form distinct stages within ordinary capacity.

The fourth con row is necessary because the epistemic burden, causal-emergence constructive, interaction-asymmetry reply, and design-relevance reply are four distinct motion-level obligations paired with three different pro answers.
The opening parity proposal is answered by the causal deduction and the initial efficient-cause symmetry breaker.

Four con rows are preauthorized because field constraints, explanatory reasons without efficient causes, the material-only transformation case, and the final parity consequence are independently assessable developments; the two pro rows answer the field warrant and clarify the any-cause scope.
Regress termination, the physical/nonmetric alternative, and the instability reply form one compact exchange.
The constructive agency derivation, no-deliberation answer, nonmetric-withholding objection, and modal-control answer are distinct but remain within ordinary capacity.

correctionRationale.summary: The correction preserves all 34 original move IDs, adds one source-required Linford reply, replaces the two overloaded topical bins with coherent paired exchanges, narrows all nine over-target spans, and removes non-exact or recognition-corrupted quotation candidates without using corrected audio wording as caption text.
semanticChanges: Observational and nonmetric arguments are grouped because both concern the inference from accessible or finite-looking history to a global beginning; the epistemic burden moves to the motion-relevance section to keep four con cards.
Causal scope and design relevance are grouped as motion-level limits on what physical causation or design of order establishes; every linked pro/con exchange remains together.
The former causal/material section is divided between the opening causal-principle symmetry breaker and the later material-parity, reason, causal-type, and scope clarifications.
The former first-cause/agency section is divided between regress/physical-scope and agency/control, preserving the chronological argumentative targets.

Linford's events 2616–2631 objection is added because it specifically challenges the intelligibility of withholding in nonmetric time and is answered by Loke's later modal-control account; it is not a repetition of the earlier physical-first-cause alternative.
